newsitem.title: CANADA: Rayrock to mothball Nevada Dee gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Rayrock to mothball Nevada Dee gold mine.

text.p: Rayrock Yellowknife Resource Inc said on Friday its higher-cost Dee Mine in northern Nevada will be put on a care and maintenance basis due to low gold prices.

Rayrock said operations at the mine will be gradually reduced during 1997, allowing Rayrock to mine and process gold ore already stripped. About 25,000 ounces of gold will be produced by the time operations are suspended in the third quarter of 1997.
The mine's current complement of 89 employees will be reduced to eight by the end of the year, Rayrock said.

"We are taking this prudent measure to protect our mid- to long-term interest in the Dee property," said Rayrock Chairman David Crombie. "With the gold price below US$350, our existing long-term expansion plan is not economic."

"The Dee property, however, has reserves of about 400,000 ounces of recoverable gold at US$400 an ounce and significant deep exploration potential. As such, we will be evaluating a broad range of long-term options," Crombie added.
The mine is located on the Carlin trend in Nevada. Rayrock has a long-term lease on the property, which is jointly owned by Franco-Nevada Mining Corp and Euro-Nevada Mining Corp.
